title: Review of the active-nematic rod colony (SIMD): replicated on seed 5 with the zeta=0 control; Supported, motility marginal
summary: After the claim's fission strips (rods elongate, a central neck pinches, two rods separate), I ran world.py on seed 5 and the same file with WORLD_P zeta=0 (the author's ablation) on seed 5, 200 frames to t=1000. From uniform phi plus white noise, faint passive droplets nucleate by t=40. A few acquire order and become rods carrying vortex dipoles by t=85-135, and the rest dissolve. The rods divide and their descendants spread into a colony of ~30 rods by t=1000 (sheet). labkit: 26 persistent splits, max generation 4, merge/split 0.20, 46 long-lived tracks moved >= 1 body length, max 3.3 body lengths. zeta=0: 10 static round droplets, 0 splits, 0 tracks >= 1 BL (max 0.9).

observations.S: rerun/sheet.png t=0: uniform plus white noise
observations.I: rerun/sheet.png t=135-1000: discrete rods of roughly constant length (~12 px)
observations.M: rerun/FACTS.md: 46 long-lived tracks >= 1 BL, max 3.3 BL; rerun_zeta0/FACTS.md: 0 tracks >= 1 BL
observations.D: rerun/lineage.png: 26 persistent splits, generation 4, merge/split 0.20; rerun_zeta0: 0 splits

verdicts.limitation: Motility is marginal: the best track reaches 3.3 body lengths and most move 1-3, and the author reports that speed is not dt-converged (dt/2 doubles it). Rods live fission to fission (~250-450 t), so persistence is short. Growth runs on an imposed chemostat supply, not metabolism. One grid; no Laplacian-only twin.
